articles.title: Tennessee Defeats Michigan State, Shakes Up AP Top 25 Rankings
articles.summary: Tennessee's stingy defense led to a dismal performance by Michigan State, who made just 18% of their shots from the floor.
articles.content: Tennessee Volunteers have handed Michigan State a resounding defeat in their last game, sending shockwaves through the AP Top 25 poll rankings. The Spartans' first stint at No. 2 this season has been short-lived, as they suffered a dismal performance on the court against the Volunteers. This loss marks a historically bad offensive outing for Michigan State, with the team making just 18% of their shots from the floor - a statistic that pales in comparison to their previous performances since 1938-39. Tennessee's stingy defense was instrumental in Michigan State's downfall, holding them to an abysmal 9 out of 50 shooting record. This feat is particularly noteworthy, as it marks the first time since 1949 that a top-20 team has failed to reach double-digit made field goals in a game. Under coach Tom Izzo, this is only the third instance where his Spartans have struggled to make 15 field goals. The Volunteers' defense proved to be an insurmountable hurdle for Michigan State's offense, with Tennessee holding their opponents to under 25% shooting - a feat they've achieved eight times under coach Rick Barnes. However, it's worth noting that this is the first time in the modern era that the Volunteers have managed to keep an opponent below the 20% mark. Tennessee's defense has long been a hallmark of the program under Rick Barnes' leadership, but this season's team presented an unusual challenge due to its high number of transfers and focus on offense. The Volunteers' revamped roster seemed poised to struggle on the defensive end, especially after a lackluster performance in their exhibition loss at Duke. However, it appears that Barnes has managed to coax his typical elite defense from the new-look team. Michigan State's starters had a dismal shooting night, combining for just three made field goals out of 28 attempts. What's more striking is that they didn't attempt a single two-point shot throughout the game. The Spartans' struggles at the rim were compounded by their inability to make shots from anywhere else on the court, with only one of their final 32 attempts going in. The Volunteers' defense has proven to be a force to be reckoned with this season, and their win over Michigan State is a testament to that. But can they sustain such a high level of play throughout the campaign? Only time will tell. Michigan State's upset victory over Duke last week was seen as a major statement, but it appears that may have been more of an anomaly than a sign of things to come. The Spartans' performance against Tennessee suggests that their earlier win might not be as impressive as thought. The loss on the road to top-15 opponent Tennessee is certainly a setback for Michigan State, and it's hard to ignore the warning signs from this defeat. A week ago, the team was riding high after beating Duke in a head-turning result, but those vibes have shifted abruptly. Michigan State struggled to find its rhythm against Tennessee, with Jasiah Jervis going 0-for-10 on the night, epitomizing the team's difficulties. Despite having made shots from anywhere else on the court just a week prior, nothing came easily for the Spartans in this game, making it a tough pill to swallow. articles.content: Mauricio Pochettino's tenure as USMNT coach has come to an end after a two-year spell that saw both progress and disappointment. The Argentine left a lasting impact on the program despite not advancing deeper at the World Cup. In his final game with the team, a 2-0 victory over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals, Pochettino's emotions were palpable as he reflected on leaving behind a tight-knit group of players. He acknowledged that when the game ended, his mind began to wander to other things, and it was tough to process the finality of it all. Pochettino is known for being passionate about people and soccer, and his decision to join Manchester United was seen as purely business-driven. However, his genuine affection for the players and staff made his goodbye a more emotional affair than initially expected. The outpouring of emotions was palpable as Mauricio Pochettino bid farewell to his USMNT family. It's impossible not to cry when you care deeply about people and they care about you, he said, highlighting the human connection that made this goodbye so bittersweet. In a poignant moment on the field, hugs and tears flowed freely among the team staff as they savored their final moments together. This emotional goodbye was far from business as usual, a testament to Pochettino's genuine affection for his players and colleagues. The final moments of Pochettino's tenure were marked by a sense of closure and satisfaction for the players. Pochettino himself acknowledged that he had wanted to leave on a positive note, one that would be remembered fondly by his team. A key factor in this was the team's ability to express themselves freely on the pitch, playing with a fluidity and creativity that brought joy to everyone involved. Pulisic's bicycle kick stood out in particular, an audacious piece of skill that caught the eye. Mauricio Pochettino reflected on his tenure as USMNT coach, expressing regret that he didn't have more time to prepare the team for the World Cup. Pochettino's tenure ended on a high note, with his players performing well in his final games. Despite this, he remains optimistic about the team's future prospects, believing that they will achieve great things. He has no doubt that this group of players has what it takes to succeed at the highest level. The US Soccer Federation has begun searching for Pochettino's replacement, who will take charge after his departure. articles.title: Trev Alberts Leaves Texas A&M to Become Michigan Athletic Director
articles.summary: Texas A&M's athletic director Trev Alberts has left his position to take on a similar role at Michigan, according to sources.
articles.content: Texas A&M's athletic director Trev Alberts has left his position to take on a similar role at Michigan, according to sources. This move comes just under two years after he started in College Station. Alberts' tenure at Texas A&M began with high expectations following his hiring in 2021. Alberts, who was an All-American linebacker during his time at Nebraska, has had a brief but notable career as an athletic director so far. He previously worked at his alma mater for three years before moving to Texas A&M after the departure of Jimbo Fisher. At Michigan, Alberts will be tasked with stabilizing the program, which is currently reeling from controversy and poor performance on the field. The Wolverines are still recovering from a scandal that led to the firing of coach Sherrone Moore last year. Michigan's football team has struggled under new leadership, with a 5-5 record since Kyle Whittingham took over as head coach. The team also parted ways with offensive coordinator Jason Beck earlier this season, reportedly paying him $7 million in buyout. Texas A&M's Trev Alberts signed a contract extension last November, securing his position through 2032 and entitling him to over $3 million per year in compensation. The massive financial commitment was made necessary by the departure of Jimbo Fisher, who left behind a $70+ million buyout - the largest in college football history. Despite this significant burden, Alberts took swift action to stabilize the athletic department's finances, making aggressive cuts to the budget while ensuring the institution's long-term solvency. Alberts' leadership will now be put to the test at Michigan, where he faces a distinct set of challenges. The university has been marred by scandals in recent years, with former coach Jim Harbaugh at the center of two major NCAA investigations, including one centered on staff member Connor Stalions. Michigan's athletic department is desperate for stability and consistency, and Alberts will need to navigate these complex issues while also building on the success achieved under his predecessor, Warde Manuel. The departure of Trev Alberts from Texas A&M's athletic department is set to occur amidst a challenging season for coach Mike Elko, who has seen his team struggle to 4-6 and face the very real possibility of missing bowl eligibility for only the third time in two decades. This would mark another instance of instability at the top of the Aggies' administration, following the departure of two previous athletic directors: Ross Bjork, who left for Ohio State, and Scott Woodward, who took over at LSU before being let go after a tumultuous tenure that included the hiring of Brian Kelly.
